page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance features 4 vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include any local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations falling into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, reaching 455.47 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 47.24 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom quarter, while medium-model LLM prompt processing lands in the bottom decile.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile and balanced resource allocation, the D4as_v7 offers reliable general-purpose cost efficiency for workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The high single-core CPU speed makes it highly suitable for single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting. However, the lack of bundled local storage and moderate multi-threaded scaling suggest it is less optimal for heavy parallel computing or data-intensive storage workloads.
